paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks across nine language families—IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic—comparing six model configurations: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The horizontal axis represents the language families, while the vertical axis quantifies the effect, ranging from 0 to 30. Each family has a group of six bars, each corresponding to one model configuration, with error bars indicating standard deviation. The IE-Indic family exhibits the highest effects, with mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2 reaching approximately 25, and mBERT-L2 and XLM-L2 reaching around 18. In contrast, the Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. The IE-Germanic family consistently shows higher effects than IE-Romance, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic and around 15 in IE-Romance. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate, with effects around 18 and 16 respectively, while the L2 and R2 variants are significantly lower, around 2–4. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars, indicating high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bar reaches approximately 15. Overall, the chart reveals significant variation in model performance across language families and configurations, with IE-Indic and IE-Germanic showing the strongest effects, and Uralic and Isolate showing minimal impact.
